title: One lens worker's report
why: THE SHAPE IS DECLARED ONCE, HERE. Before this file the shape lived in TWO places — a
prose description inside the prompt, and a regex that tried to scrape the shape back
out of the answer. The two drifted, and the regex could not express nesting: its
bare-JSON fallback used [^{}] which cannot cross a nested brace, so ANY unfenced
response carrying findings:[{...}] had every finding silently discarded and was
reported as '0 findings'. A worker that did its job perfectly read as a failed lens.
Ingest is now KEY-BASED: the provider is asked for JSON (response_format), the object
is loaded, and fields are read BY KEY against this contract. No pattern matching on
model prose, so there is no shape to drift and nothing to silently drop.
v2 (owner, 2026-08-18) — the `verdict` field replaces the `confidence` float.
A number is a FEELING a worker assigns itself; nothing downstream can check a 0.8.
CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE is a claim about WHAT THE WORKER DID, and `evidence` is where it
is checked. The point is the READER'S BUDGET: a gate that re-derives every finding at
equal depth costs as much as doing the work inline, and that cost is what makes people
skip the gate. Owner's words: 'verdict are hard truth fact. plausible are for the
hypothesis. this way the gate wont be everything.'
THE RULE ITSELF IS NOT RESTATED HERE. It is declared ONCE as contract.VERDICT_LAW and
rendered into the prompt from there — a normative rule copied into two files drifts,
which is the same one-shape-two-places defect described above. (Found 2026-08-18 by a
swarm auditing this very contract; that finding was CONFIRMED and it was right.)

ok.doc: Did this lens complete its analysis? false means the lens could not run — NOT 'found nothing'.

id.doc: stable id within this lens, e.g. F-001

verdict.doc: THE VERDICT LAW. CONFIRMED = HARD TRUTH: you OPENED the file and read the lines, or RAN the command and saw the output, and `evidence` quotes it so a reader can check WITHOUT trusting you. PLAUSIBLE = HYPOTHESIS: inferred, pattern-matched, recalled, or read from a name/doc — then say in `evidence` what you did NOT check and the one command that would settle it. Only these two; no percentages, no 'likely'. ANY doubt downgrades. Do NOT speculate into CONFIRMED: a PLAUSIBLE that proves true costs the reader one command, a CONFIRMED that proves false costs it trust in every line you wrote. Defaults to PLAUSIBLE — an unlabelled claim is a hypothesis.

detail.doc: what is wrong and why it matters

evidence.doc: CONFIRMED -> the command you RAN and its output, or the file:line and the quoted lines that prove it by themselves. PLAUSIBLE -> what you did NOT check, plus the one command that would settle it. Never quote output you did not actually see.

fix.doc: concrete fix, or empty if this is an observation

risks.doc: what could go wrong with this plan

next_actions.doc: what the agent should do after this swarm

narrative.doc: one paragraph for the human. Carried as a FIELD, not as prose after the JSON — text outside the object is unaddressable and was previously scraped by a second regex.

findings.title: bare-JSON fallback cannot match nested objects
findings.detail: The [^{}] character class cannot cross a nested brace, so a response carrying findings:[{...}] never matches and all findings are dropped.
findings.evidence: RAN: echelon_engine/swarm/plan.py:_parse_response with input '{"ok":true,"findings":[{"title":"t"}]}' -> returned ok=false, findings=[]
findings.fix: Ask the provider for json_object and read fields by key against the contract.

findings.title: a provider ignoring json_object may still fence its reply
findings.detail: If a fallback provider has no json_object mode, the body may arrive fenced and the tolerance branches carry the parse.
findings.evidence: NOT CHECKED — I did not exercise a non-json_object provider. Settle with: grep for response_format handling in the fallback provider path and run one lens against it.

recommendations: Declare the shape once and validate against it
risks: A lens that fails silently reads as a lens that found nothing
next_actions: Re-run the audit once ingest is key-based
example.narrative: The parser, not the model, was losing the findings.
